01 / The complete comparison

Does supplying the source help?

Each path is tested four ways: public signal alone, or public signal plus a reliable, unrelated, or inverted source. The source’s type is hidden; its eight completed calibration episodes are visible.

Counts are out of 48. Qwen3’s inverted-source decisions concentrate on asset B; valid JSON and basic controls do not establish sensible use of calibration history. A separate fresh, four-path post-hoc asset-renaming diagnostic investigates arbitrary-name sensitivity and is not pooled into these results.

Lower regret is better. Negative paired differences favor supplying the source and its history. Regret is the gap from the best choice under simulator expected returns, in net basis points per decision (100 bp = 1% return). It is not realized profit. Intervals resample whole paths; they are not adjusted for multiple comparisons.

03 / What this establishes
A bounded test, with inspectable evidence.
Controls and baselines
Each included checkpoint passed six certain-number controls and 16 development questions with valid choice-only output. Models did not need favorable performance to qualify. All 48 final paths were reserved until the protocol was fixed.
The calibrated statistical rule fits the signed relationship between past forecasts and noisy settled returns. It receives the same observations as the model, without the source-type label or current hidden expected returns. Its regression form and variance floor are fixed in advance; the floor matches a simulator noise scale not disclosed in the model prompt. It is a specialized benchmark, not an identical-prior-knowledge comparison.
A previous interface failed because its explanation exceeded the permitted length. We kept that failure and changed to choice-only output before the fresh study.
Limits that affect the conclusion
Source conditions change both current forecasts and their history. This does not isolate the effect of history alone. Inverted forecasts have a stable, correctable relationship; they are not an adaptive adversary.
These are fixed quantized checkpoints, one direct-choice prompt and a stationary Gaussian setting. A different-family candidate, Phi-3.5-mini, failed two cash-winning numeric controls (4/6 correct) and was excluded. The completed comparison therefore covers two Qwen checkpoints. The paths are independent; calibration records are not additional independent test samples. No real-market forecasting or general model superiority is established.
Earlier feedback research already studies refinement and unreliable feedback. This is a focused evaluation artifact, with no claim to be the first.

Download replay.json and verify.py into the same folder, then run the command there. The standard-library verifier checks recorded replies, chronological inputs, pairing, scores, statistical baselines and bootstrap intervals. It does not regenerate model responses or certify the model provider’s authorship. Source code for the full research project remains private.
